name: Masa (Northern Rice Cakes)
summary: Fluffy, slightly tangy fermented rice pancakes with crisp edges, cooked in a hollowed pan.
story: Masa is a Hausa fermented rice cake sold in the mornings and evenings across northern Nigeria. It is cooked in a special pan with round hollows and is often eaten with spicy yaji powder, sugar or a vegetable stew.

steps.title: Soak the rice
steps.text: Wash the raw rice and soak it in cold water for 4-6 hours until you can crush a grain easily between your fingers.

steps.title: Blend the batter
steps.text: Drain the rice and blend with the cooked rice and the warm water until very smooth with no gritty bits. The batter should be thick like pancake batter.

steps.title: Ferment
steps.text: Stir in the yeast and sugar, cover and leave in a warm place for 2-4 hours. It is ready when it is bubbly, has risen and smells pleasantly sour.

steps.title: Season the batter
steps.text: Stir in the salt and baking powder and fold in the onion if using. Stir gently so the bubbles are not knocked out. Add a spoon of water if too stiff.

steps.title: Heat the pan
steps.text: Heat a masa pan, an aebleskiver pan or a cast-iron muffin tin over medium heat. Brush each hollow with oil and wait until a drop of batter sizzles.

steps.title: Cook the first side
steps.text: Fill each hollow about three-quarters with batter. Cover and cook for 3-4 minutes until the bottom is deep golden and the top is set around the edges.

steps.title: Flip and finish
steps.text: Turn each cake with a skewer or fork and cook for 2 minutes until golden all around and springy in the centre. Repeat with remaining batter, oiling the pan each time.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Eat hot, dusted with yaji, or sprinkled with sugar, or with miyan taushe or a tomato sauce.

tips: Make sure the rice is fully ground; a coarse batter gives dense masa.
Do not skip fermentation; it gives the cakes their softness and tang.
Keep the heat medium; high heat burns the outside and leaves the middle raw.
Leftover cakes reheat well in a dry pan.

swaps.swap: Use a non-stick mini muffin tin on the stove or a small frying pan for flat pancakes; the shape changes but the taste does not.
Mix ground roasted peanuts, cayenne, ginger and a pinch of stock powder; the heat and nutty flavour will be similar.
